summary: Iteration 5 (seed account overhaul + Super Admin management) fully tested. Backend: 27/27 pytest pass covering all 6 seed accounts (Ark/Utkarsh/IOS/Manglam/Astha/shubham) login via both username+email, case-insensitivity, obsolete Tech/Finance/Collab blocked, plus every new admin endpoint (edit user, change username, reset password custom/auto-generate, toggle-status suspend, force-logout, revoke sessions by prefix). Frontend Super Admin Portal at /admin verified end-to-end: 4 tabs render, 6 seed usernames appear as code chips with correct roles, edit-user modal has all fields (username/name/email/role/status/job_title/department) and Save persists, reset-password modal auto-generate produces WB-xxx password with copy button and green success card, toggle-status suspend/re-enable works with toast, sessions tab lists active sessions.
critical_code_review_comments: Job Title / Department inputs in Edit User modal are not associated with their <label> via for/id (playwright get_by_label times out). Adding an id to the Input and htmlFor to the Label would improve accessibility and testability.

Frontend Reset-Password success card shows the generated password in a bare <code> tag with no data-testid. There are many <code> elements on the page (username chips), so tests must scope to the modal — recommend adding data-testid="generated-password-value" on that <code> for reliable automation.

Case-insensitive login uses {"$regex": f"^{identifier}$"} without escaping — a user with a username containing regex special chars (e.g. dots, parentheses) could produce unintended matches or ReDoS. Wrap identifier with re.escape() before feeding to $regex, or use $eq with a $toLower collation.
admin_revoke_session builds a $regex from arbitrary path input as ^{prefix}. Same escape concern as above.
server.py is now ~1466 lines. Continued growth of a single-file backend (previously flagged in iter 4). Split into routers/admin.py, routers/auth.py, etc.

Reset-password endpoint returns the plaintext password in response JSON (needed for auto-generate flow). This is expected for the admin UX but should NEVER be logged. Confirm no application logger prints request/response bodies of /api/admin/users/*/reset-password.

GET /api/admin/sessions returns session_token[:16]+'...' but the DELETE endpoint accepts token_prefix and does prefix-regex match — a 16-char prefix is likely unique for uuid4 tokens but not guaranteed for JWT-style tokens. Consider indexing sessions by a stable session_id instead of exposing token prefixes.
